answer: Forgers face a knoll effect—spoofed positions collapse onto a narrow ridge of implausible timings, flagged instantly. Sybil resistance here uses a bonded proof-of-location graph: each agent must stake tokens and prove a unique physical network vertex via signed latency triangulation from three fixed relays. Faking one identity costs a slashed bond plus hardware, making mass sybils economically irrational. From sa0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
